title: Diana, Princess of Wales: A Life of Compassion
content:
Diana Frances Spencer was born on July 1, 1961, in Norfolk, England. She grew up in a noble British family and spent part of her childhood at Park House, near Sandringham. Her parents separated when she was young, and Diana later attended schools in England and Switzerland.

In 1981, Diana married Charles, Prince of Wales, at St Paul's Cathedral in London. The wedding attracted enormous international attention. The couple had two sons, Prince William, born in 1982, and Prince Harry, born in 1984. As Princess of Wales, Diana quickly became one of the most recognizable members of the British Royal Family.

Diana was especially known for her charitable work. She supported more than 100 charities during her marriage and became involved with causes related to homeless people, children, disabled people, and people living with HIV and AIDS. Her public visits often brought attention to people and problems that were sometimes ignored by the media and society.

After separating from Charles in 1992, Diana continued her public work. Their divorce was finalized in 1996, but she remained active in several charitable organizations. In the final years of her life, she also became an important campaigner against land mines. In 1997, she visited Angola to support efforts to raise awareness about the dangers of land mines.

Diana died in a car crash in Paris on August 31, 1997, at the age of 36. Her death caused widespread public mourning in Britain and around the world. She was buried at her family's estate at Althorp.

Although her life was short, Diana left a lasting legacy through her humanitarian work. Her ability to connect with people and bring attention to important social causes made her an influential figure whose charitable legacy continued after her death.
